text:
This looks like mid-2008. Fed funds are at 2.01%, which fits after the cuts to 2.00% in April 2008. Headline CPI at 3.88% fits May 2008 (it was 4.2% in May and 3.98% in April, with March at 3.98%), so the CPI figure points to roughly April–May. The 2-year yield rose 1.02 points over 3 months, from about 1.65% in March to 2.67%, which fits May 2008 (2y around 2.6–2.7%). The 10-year at 4.08% in May 2008 is also about right.

Unemployment of 5.0% matches April–May 2008 (5.0% in April, 5.5% in June). Payrolls averaging -61k fit as well. US equities returned +1.5% over the month, consistent with May 2008 (S&P +1.3%). Gold at +0.9% for the month fits May too.

CPI of 3.88% fits April better, since April CPI was 3.9% and May was 4.2%. Treasuries fell 1.8% in the month, which fits May, when yields rose sharply. The 3-month VIX change of -8.4 fits May, with VIX around 18 against about 26 in March.

The best estimate is May 2008. The CPI for May was released in June, so the CPI may be lagged and still show April's 3.9%.
